change_types.text: A new function, class, component, hook, module, command or file convention that did not exist before. Not an implementation catching up with a standard or a documented API (a missing or broken constructor, method or property now provided): that is a fix.
A new option, flag, parameter, argument or configuration key on something that already exists.
Existing code or configuration now behaves differently at run time or build time (not only a default value, not a bug fix).
The default value of an existing option, setting or mode changed.
A bug fix: wrong results, crashes, errors or regressions corrected, restoring intended, standard or documented behaviour.
Something still works but is marked for future removal (a warning, a deprecation notice).
Something that existed was removed or no longer works, including dropped support for a runtime or platform version.
An API or feature moved between experimental, preview, beta, unstable and stable.
Faster, or less memory, CPU, network, queries or bundle size, with nothing new to write.
Closes a vulnerability or hardens a default or an API against misuse or attack.
Developer tooling: the CLI, build tooling, codemods, dev server, type generation, test or editor tooling.

surfaces.text: Application code calls, imports, implements or extends it (functions, classes, components, decorators, hooks).
A configuration file or object, a setting, an environment variable.
A file or directory name or location the framework recognises (proxy.ts, app/ routes, schema.prisma location).
A command, subcommand or flag typed in a terminal or a package.json script.
A database schema, a data model definition, or a migration.
TypeScript types only; nothing changes at run time.
Running code behaves differently; there is nothing for a project to write.
The build, bundler, compiler or dev server output and behaviour.

benefits.text: Closes a vulnerability, or hardens a default or an API against misuse or attack.
Prevents wrong results, data loss, crashes, hangs or other bugs in a project that uses this.
Makes a project faster, or use less memory, CPU, network, queries or bundle size.
Lowers what running the project costs (compute, storage, paid API usage, infrastructure).

Replaces code a project would otherwise write and maintain itself (a hand-rolled helper, workaround or wrapper, or a third-party package used for the same job) with a supported built-in. Only when the record names, or `replaces` lists, what it supersedes; not for a new capability, and not for a rename.

benefit_rule: Answer yes only where the record's summary or evidence states this benefit, or it is the documented purpose of the feature. Do not infer gains the source does not claim. New conveniences, ergonomics, naming, style, type-only changes, tooling preferences, optional modernisation and new capabilities without this benefit are no.
breaking_rubric: BREAKING (yes) means: a project that worked on the previous version, upgraded to this release with no change to its code, configuration, scripts or tooling, then fails (an error, a failed build or type check, a command that no longer exists) or behaves differently in a way its users or developers would notice. Raising a minimum supported version of a runtime or dependency is breaking. A removal is breaking.

NOT BREAKING (no) includes: a new optional feature or option; a deprecation that still works (a warning only); a recommendation or optional modernisation ("we recommend", "you may", "not required", new project defaults that existing projects need not adopt); a fix that restores documented behaviour; documentation changes.
Judge what the change does to existing code, not where it is listed. If the source does not show that existing code stops working or changes behaviour, answer no.

questions.change_type: What kind of change is this? Pick the one type that fits best.
questions.surface: Where does a project that uses this technology meet this change? Pick the one surface that fits best.
questions.benefit: Does this change bring a %BENEFIT% benefit? %BENEFIT%: %DEFINITION% %RULE%
